clue.text: The head being held in disrespect is a danger signal

indicators.note: the phrase says one piece is gripped inside another, so the word for disrespect wraps around the head

parts.note: a slight is an act of disrespect or snub
the top is the head of something, as the head of a page

explanation.surface: A gesture of contempt with the head is a warning sign of trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disrespect' looks like part of the definition's picture but supplies the outer word, and 'being held in' places the head inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A red traffic lamp ordering drivers to halt is a warning signal on the road.

clue.text: Split involving the Right in stupid blunder

indicators.note: involving means taking something in, so the abbreviation for right goes inside the jumbled letters
to blunder is to stumble about clumsily, so the letters of the word stupid get knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A political party splits when its right wing makes a foolish mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blunder' rearranges STUPID to DISUPT; 'involving' places R within it.
explanation.definitionFit: To break apart or throw into disorder is to cause a split, as a quarrel does to a group.

clue.text: The artist would put crimson first

parts.note: crimson is a colour, a deep red
first is written 1ST, with the figure 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A painter would choose red before any other shade.
explanation.walkthrough: First is abbreviated 1st, and setters often read the figure 1 as the letter I, giving IST.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter or designer especially skilled in the handling of hues is called by this name.

clue.text: Meaning to support the Opposition leader, give voice

indicators.note: 'to' puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: pro means in support of, for

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of Opposition

parts.note: to give voice is to sing

explanation.surface: A politician intends to back the opposition chief and speak up for them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' takes the O at the start of Opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: Intending, as in planning to do something, is a sense shared with putting forward a plan.

clue.text: Get through short run in a bit

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for run inside the word for a bit

parts.note: a piece is a bit or portion
R is the short form of run, as on cricket scorecards

explanation.surface: Making a short dash in a small portion of time gets you through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short run' is the cricket scoring abbreviation; 'in' places it within the word for a bit.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce is to bore or penetrate, getting through a surface.

clue.text: A help to the old writer in making his point

definitions.text: A help to the old writer in making his point

parts.words: A help to the old writer in making his point
parts.note: the point is literal: writers using quills once needed a small blade to sharpen the nib, which gave the tool its name

explanation.surface: Something aided a writer of old in arguing his case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making his point' sounds like arguing, but it means sharpening the tip of a quill pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A small folding pocket blade was originally used for cutting and trimming quill pens.

clue.text: Catches up with an undoubtedly tough guy

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from the bottom, so the letters of the word for catches run backwards

parts.note: traps catches, as of animals
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hard man catches up with somebody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the word for catches, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Citizens of ancient Sparta were famous for hardiness, so a person of austere toughness takes their name.

clue.text: No single part appears offensive

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one, a single
some is a part or portion of a whole

explanation.surface: Not one section of something looks objectionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Noxious and disgusting, especially of a smell, is the sense here.

clue.text: Slip on oil-spillage in the city

parts.note: to trip is to slip or stumble

indicators.note: a spillage scatters things about, so the letters of oil are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone slips on spilt oil somewhere in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spillage' rearranges OIL to OLI. Tripoli is the capital of Libya.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripoli is the capital of Libya, and also a city in Lebanon.

clue.text: Remedy for the worker taken by a body of policemen

parts.note: an ant is the crossword worker, after the worker ants of a colony
the CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of British police

explanation.surface: A labourer is arrested by a squad of detectives.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of a British police force.
explanation.definitionFit: A medicine that neutralises stomach acid is a remedy for indigestion.

clue.text: Hit back and glower, but make room

indicators.note: back means the word for hit is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to rap is to hit sharply
to lour is to scowl or glower

explanation.surface: Strike back and scowl, but give way to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns RAP to PAR. LOUR (also spelt lower) means to frown.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitting room in a house, especially for receiving visitors, is the sense.

clue.text: With private transport, folk will be in the pink!

parts.note: a car is private transport
a nation is a people or folk

explanation.surface: A people with their own cars will be in great health and good spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the pink' means in fine health, but here the pink is the garden flower family to which the answer belongs.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinks are the Dianthus flowers, and this cultivated bloom is one of them.

clue.text: A goddess merits a break

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to break something is to smash it into pieces, so the letters of merits are rearranged

explanation.surface: A goddess has earned some time off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A goddess' at the front is the definition; the A that opens the answer is the second 'a', and 'break' shuffles only 'merits'.
explanation.definitionFit: Artemis was the Greek deity of the hunt and the moon.

clue.text: The man bringing in intimate letters for the queen

parts.note: to intimate is to suggest or import a meaning
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the monarch's cipher

explanation.surface: Someone delivers private letters meant for Her Majesty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intimate' is the verb, to hint or signify, as import also means.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader who brings goods in from abroad is the person described.

clue.text: Used foil — within limits

definitions.meaning: to have wielded a foil is to have practised swordplay
enclosed by a boundary, like a field with railings

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is having sparred with swords; the other is enclosed by railings or a boundary.

clue.text: Looked on as a bloomer by people in the Alps

definitions.text: Looked on as a bloomer by people in the Alps

parts.words: Looked on as a bloomer by people in the Alps
parts.note: a bloomer sounds like a blunder, but here it is literally a flower, one mountain dwellers treasure

explanation.surface: Alpine folk regard something as a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' is British slang for a blunder; here it is a flowering plant of the Alps.
explanation.definitionFit: This white woolly flower grows high in the Alps and is a symbol of Austria and Switzerland.

clue.text: Gloomy newspapers indeed!

indicators.note: the word indeed is split so that in tells us the press goes inside the remaining word deed

parts.note: taken as written
the press is a collective word for newspapers

explanation.surface: An exclamation that the papers are gloomy indeed.
explanation.walkthrough: The solver must split 'indeed' into 'in deed', taking 'in' as the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Low in spirits and dejected is what being gloomy means.

clue.text: Children holding a cleric back should be parted

indicators.note: holding means the word for children keeps something inside it

parts.note: seed means offspring or children, in the biblical sense

indicators.note: back means the word for a cleric is read in reverse

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a cleric

explanation.surface: Children clutching a clergyman should be pulled apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns REV to VER, and 'holding' puts it in the middle of the word for children.
explanation.definitionFit: Cut off or separated, as of a limb or a tie, is to be parted.

clue.text: See a note to a girl as a means of making things clear

definitions.text: a means of making things clear

parts.note: to eye something is to see or look at it
G is a note of the musical scale
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: Look at a letter sent to a young woman to clear things up.
explanation.definitionFit: A single lens such as a monocle helps the wearer see sharply.

clue.text: Strive to encompass feed contract

indicators.note: to encompass is to surround, so the word for strive wraps around the word for feed

parts.note: to try is to strive or attempt
to eat is to feed

explanation.surface: Struggle to cover a catering agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strive' and 'feed' read as verbs in the surface; 'to encompass' wraps one around the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal agreement between nations is a binding contract.

clue.text: Blame for every upset on journey

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the word for every upside down so it reads from the bottom

parts.note: per means for every, as in miles per hour
to rove is to journey or wander

explanation.surface: Fault is found for every disturbance on a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns PER to REP, reading from the bottom in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To reprove someone is to rebuke or censure them, to find fault.

clue.text: New mate ill-disposed to make it for ever

indicators.note: something new is made afresh, so the letters of mate and ill are put together in a fresh order
disposed means arranged or set out, so the letters of mate and ill are laid out again

explanation.surface: A new partner, unfriendly, means to make it last for ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' and 'disposed' both signal the one rearrangement of MATE and ILL; 'ill-disposed' poses as hostility in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-time record or high is the greatest ever, unsurpassed at any period.

clue.text: Stronger drink may be taken with a certain hesitation

parts.note: stout is a dark beer, a drink
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A strong drink may be accepted with some hesitancy.
explanation.walkthrough: Stout is a dark beer such as Guinness.
explanation.definitionFit: Stout means sturdy and strong, so its comparative means stronger or more robust.

clue.text: One really admires properly tailored characters

indicators.note: the letters of tailored are set properly, in the right order to give a new word

explanation.surface: A real admirer of nicely cut clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'properly' rearranges the letters of TAILORED; 'characters' just means letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A worshipper of idols, or a devoted admirer of someone, is the sense here.

clue.text: A minister has some latitude — a considerable amount

indicators.note: some means a portion, so part of the run of letters in latitude a considerable is taken

explanation.surface: A clergyman has quite a bit of freedom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes letters from the end of 'latitude' across 'a' into 'considerable'.
explanation.definitionFit: A deacon is an ordained minister in the church, below a priest.

clue.text: A game fighter's point taken, express contrition

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback
a GI is an American soldier, a fighter, and the possessive gives an S
E is a point of the compass, east

explanation.surface: A combative polo player concedes the point and says sorry.
explanation.walkthrough: GI is an American soldier; the possessive 's gives an S.
explanation.definitionFit: To say sorry is to show contrition.

clue.text: Entrances a lovely woman going around European capital

indicators.note: going around means the word for a lovely woman surrounds a letter

parts.note: a Venus is a beautiful woman, after the Roman goddess of love

indicators.note: a capital is a first, upper-case letter, so the first letter of European is taken

explanation.surface: A beauty travelling round a European capital enchants us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrances' looks like a verb, to enchant; it is the noun, ways in. 'capital' takes the E of European, which 'going around' puts inside VENUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Avenues are approaches or ways in, as in avenues of inquiry.

clue.text: Company settling claim found amusing

indicators.note: settling is putting things in order, so the letters of claim are rearranged

explanation.surface: A firm settled a claim and found it funny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settling' rearranges CLAIM to MICAL; 'settling claim' poses as an insurance payout.
explanation.definitionFit: Funny or laughable is the shared sense.

clue.text: Broad Russian river view

parts.note: the Ob is a long river in Siberia
a scene is a view

explanation.surface: A wide Russian river view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broad' looks like wide, but it means coarse or indecent, as broad humour.
explanation.definitionFit: Broad in the sense of coarse or indecent humour matches lewd and offensive.

clue.text: Touching and yielding in decline

parts.note: re means concerning or touching on, as in business letters
a cession is a yielding or surrender, as of territory

explanation.surface: Being affected and giving in leads to a downturn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touching' is the old sense meaning concerning, which is RE.
explanation.definitionFit: An economic slump is a decline in trade and activity.
